newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Nail, Rembrandt target GSFA.
newsitem.headline: Nail, Rembrandt target GSFA.

text.p: Black empowerment business group New Africa Investment Ltd said on Thursday it was in talks with Rembrandt Group Ltd to take control of Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd, the world's third largest gold producer.

In a cautionary notice to shareholders, Nail said it was in dicussions with Gold Fields and its Driefontein Consolidated Ltd unit to acquire their shareholdings in Asteroid Ltd, which holds 40 percent of GFSA Holdings Ltd.
"The successful conclusion of these discussions would result in a partnership being formed between Rembrandt Group Ltd and Nail in GFSA Holdings Ltd," it said.

Industry sources had told Reuters late on Wednesday that discussions were in progress for Nail, headed by former African National Congress sceretary-general Cyril Ramaphosa, to acquire an interest in Gold Fields.

The deal, if successful, would mark a further big advance for black business in South Africa -- and a significant coup for Nail which already has control of industrial group Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd.

Gold Fields would provide a major presence in the mining industry, something Nail is believed to be keen to achieve. Nail had been seen as a potential bidder for a stake in rival mining house JCI Ltd, but that deal was finally clinched by another black empowerment consortium, African Mining Group, led by Capital Alliance Holdings Ltd.
Business Day newspaper quoted Gold Fields finance director John Hopwood as saying that the deal would result in the transfer to Nail of an effective 17.2 percent of Gold Fields.

Discussions could take several months and would hinge on two key issues -- the price for the combined effective 40 percent stake that Gold Fields and Driefontein hold in GFSA Holdings via equally-owned Asteroid; and the structure which would allow the deal to take take place.
Asteroid, with its 40 percent stake in GFSA Holdings, is the key to the deal since GFSA Holdings, in turn, owns 43 percent of operating company Gold Fields.

A price of about 1.8 billion rand was the benchmark for the Nail deal, based on market valuation, said Hopwood. Gold Fields shares closed at 109.75 rand on Wednesday. The question of a premium being paid is expected to be one of the points under discussion.

Industry sources said the deal being structured would give Nail and Rembrandt 34.4 percent control in Gold Fields in an equal split. Their joint stake would amount to some 3.5 billion rand based on current market values.

Rembrandt already has a significant stake in Gold Fields via its 40 percent holding in GFSA Holdings. The remaining shares in GFSA Holdings are split between the 40 percent held by Asteroid and 20 percent held by Liberty Life.
Gold Fields produced 23.45 tonnes of gold in the quarter to end-March when it made an after-tax profit of 236.42 million rand before capital expenditure.
